To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The LysM pathway is a major source of methionine for E. coli. (2) The LysR regulon is involved in the regulation of the LysM pathway.
the lysine and methionine biosynthetic pathways are interconnected and that a mutation in one pathway can affect the other.

the lysine and methionine auxotrophs of Escherichium coli K12 were isolated, the mutants were shown to be defective in the enzymes lipoic acid synthase, alpha-ketogluterate dehydrogenases, and the enzymes involved in the biosynthesis of lipoic acid were purified.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation and characterization of mutants of E. coli K-12 which are deficient in the enzymes of the pyruvate dehydrogenate complex and with the isolation of a mutant which requires lysine plus methionine for growth.
the isolation and characterization of mutants of E. coli which require lypoic acid, acetatesuccinate, or lysinemethionine for aerobic gowth with glucose.
the isolation of mutants that are deficient in the ability to synthesize lipoic acid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lip mutants of E. coli have an impaired ability to grow on glucose in the presence of oxygen.
the lipoic acid biosynthetic pathway in E. coli K12 has been elucidated.

, although there are a large number of lysine auxotrophs of E. coli which are unable to grow in the absence of added lysine, only a very small number of these mutants are defective in the ability to synthesize lysine from the precursor amino acid pool.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
lipoic acid plays an important role in the regulation of the alpha-keto glutarate dehydrogenases.
the lysine+methionine requirement was due to a defect in alpha-ketogluterate dehydrogenese.
we have identified a new class of E. coli mutants that are deficient in lipoic acid synthesis, have a defect in the alpha-ketogluterate dehydrogenases and have a defect in methionine metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many ways to get a mutant, and that you can get a lot of information from the mutant you get.
we can now identify and study the molecular basis for the regulation of the genes encoding the lipoic acid biosynthesis enzymes.
the lipoic acid synthesis pathway is not essential in E. coli.
